newsitem.title: USA: Rock-Tenn to buy Waldorf, creating folding carton giant.
newsitem.headline: Rock-Tenn to buy Waldorf, creating folding carton giant.

text.p: Rock-Tenn Co. said Friday it has agreed to buy Waldorf Corp. for about $410 million including assumption of debt, a deal that would create the second-largest producer of folding cartons in North America.
Rock-Tenn said it would also most likely be the biggest producer of 100 percent recycled paperboard, excluding containerboard and gypsum board, with capacity to produce almost 1 million tons a year.
The deal is the largest step so far in Rock-Tenn's plan to grow through strategic acquisitions in the consolidating packaging and paperboard industry.

"Together we will cover North America with a broad network of folding carton and recycled paperboard manufacturing operations, one splendid sales force and the widest variety of production capability in the industry today," said Bradley Currey Jr., chairman and chief executive of Rock-Tenn.
Under the tentative agreement, Rock-Tenn Co. will acquire the outstanding stock of the privately owned parent of Waldorf. The price includes cash and debt assumed.
Atlanta-based Rock-Tenn is a leading producer of packaging and recycled paperboard products, with 63 manufacturing and distribution operations in the United States and Canada.

Waldorf, based in St. Paul, Minn., makes folding cartons, recycled paperboard and other materials for some of North America's largest users of packaging. With about 2,000 employees at 10 plants in the Midwest, Northeast and the South, it earned $17.4 million on sales of $377 million in the year ended June 30, the companies said.

Rock-Tenn said it plans to finance the deal with cash and borrowings under a new $400 million credit facility. It plans to repay part of the debt with net proceeds of a public stock offering early in 1997.
The acquisition is expected to close in January, subject to execution of a definitive agreement and approval by regulators.
Rock-Tenn stock fell 50 cents to $19 in early trading on Nasdaq.
